main_text.p: Solis, addit: Quod vero ad descensionem attinet, facile ex adscensione potes eam cernere. Nam haec est differentia, quod in adscensu Tinctura ante acquirit, quam corpus: hic vero (scilicet in descensu) citius amittit. Itaq; metalla (inquit) descendentia multo sunt imperfectiora, quam adscendentia: Haec ille. Proinde ubinam semen & Tinctura frugifera vel infrugifera sit in metallis, eadem septuria prima cap. 2. de semine metallorum in hanc sententiam scribens, Adscensio (inquit) & descensio metallorum fieri non posset, nisi in semine convenirent, & sibi invicem cognata essent. Item, Argentum & aurum habent idem semen (inquit) quod in adscensu argentum transmutat in aurum: in descensu vero transfert in cuprum. Deniq; eodem

page.notes: Transcription uncertain in places: "septuria" may be "septima" or "septuaginta" in the printed text; the printer's "Tinctura" spelling and the long-s forms have been copied as they appear. The final line "odem" is set flush right and is probably the word "eodem" split across the line end; the word "e-" at the line end and "odem" below are kept as printed.
